name: Dinosaur Jr.
label: SST
lede: Three kids from Amherst, Massachusetts got banned from nearly every club around for volume, made to add a "Jr." by a band of ex-Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane members, and fell out so badly that Lou Barlow wrote about it for years. Then J Mascis and Barlow reunited, and the second run made more albums than the first.

hero.by: Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Le Trabendo, Paris, October 2022)

eras.title: Deep Wound ends, Mogo lasts one night
eras.text: Mascis and Barlow met as hardcore kids in Amherst, with Mascis on drums. When hardcore started to feel narrow, Mascis moved to guitar and wrote songs that stunned Barlow, then quietly dumped his first singer after a single show.

years.h: An ad for someone who could play really fast
years.p: J Mascis answers it and becomes the drummer in Lou Barlow's high school hardcore band, [[Deep Wound|7cee4e5d-8ea4-48fb-a7e2-c3adcc543f81]]. Barlow plays guitar.

years.h: With Deep Wound over, Mascis picks up a guitar
years.p: He starts writing his own songs and asks [[Lou Barlow|6523f86d-11d3-489e-81f6-6cbe08c367de]] to play bass. Barlow later called the songs brilliant, far beyond his own.
years.xp: Wikipedia says both had drifted toward slower, heavier music, including Black Sabbath and the Replacements, and hardcore had stopped holding their interest.

years.h: Mogo's first show ends with the singer yelling at the police
years.p: At UMass Amherst, Charlie Nakajima turns the set by Mascis, Barlow and drummer [[Murph|9d47f849-23c5-4a9f-88eb-db2774595bf8]] into an anti-police tirade. Mascis ends Mogo the next day.
years.xp:
Mascis admitted he was too wimpy to fire Nakajima outright. He re-formed the band with Barlow and Murph and simply didn't tell Nakajima.

The new trio called itself Dinosaur, with Mascis and Barlow splitting lead vocals.

eras.title: Banned in Amherst, taken on tour by Sonic Youth
eras.text: Dinosaur's volume cost it the local clubs, but Sonic Youth heard something else and took the band on the road. By the end of 1987 it had left Homestead for SST, which put out two albums, with a lawyer's letter and a guitar fight along the way.

years.h: Dinosaur costs $500 and sells 1,500 copies
years.p: Cut at a home studio outside Northampton for [[Gerard Cosloy|b3c600d5-e1dd-4525-855d-6d4f950c3be6]]'s Homestead label. Barlow sings many of the leads because Mascis isn't yet comfortable singing.
years.xp: Cosloy, a college friend of Mascis, had left UMass Amherst to run Homestead and promised to put out an album if Mascis made one. The record got almost no press.

years.h: One club around Amherst and Northampton still books them
years.p: Murph told SPIN the band got banned from nearly every club in the area but one. People left rooms to get away from the volume.
years.xp: Hypebot's history has the band working its way out to Boston, Hoboken and New York, with shows at CBGB, the Channel and Maxwell's.

years.h: Sonic Youth keep coming back, then invite them on tour
years.p: Unimpressed at first, [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] saw Dinosaur several times, turned into fans, and took them across the Northeast and northern Midwest.
years.xp: Hypebot says an opening slot for Big Black at Maxwell's in Hoboken is what got Sonic Youth's attention.

years.h: Mascis skips a Homestead deal for Greg Ginn's SST
years.p: Homestead boss Gerard Cosloy felt betrayed when Mascis passed on a two-album deal. Mascis then moved to New York, and Barlow and Murph felt left behind.
years.xp:
Cosloy, quoted on Wikipedia: "There was no way I couldn't take it personally."

The label Mascis chose was run by [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]].

years.h: SST No. 130 is You're Living All Over Me
years.p: Engineered by [[Wharton Tiers|de3636ee-5022-462b-b427-34be9674f281]] in New York. Mascis dictated Murph's every drumbeat; Barlow got two songs, Lose and Poledo, the second sung over his ukulele.
years.xp:
Mascis has called it his favorite Dinosaur Jr. album. Pitchfork put it at No. 40 on its 1980s list, and it has been called the first perfect indie rock album.

Magnet describes SST being convinced a technical problem had wrecked the master tape. Mascis assured the label it was supposed to sound that way.

His explanation: "I had been a drummer, so I wanted the guitar to have the effect of drums, to move air."

years.h: A band of sixties veterans makes them add "Jr."
years.p: Dinosaurs, with ex-members of the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane, Quicksilver and Country Joe and the Fish, sent a cease and desist. SST recalled early copies of the new LP credited to Dinosaur.
years.xp:
Dinosaurs included [[Robert Hunter|e9b419b5-ab8f-425c-8214-a7259e6efe10]], Spencer Dryden, Peter Albin of Big Brother and the Holding Company, John Cipollina and Barry Melton. They had formed in California in 1982 and broke up in 1989.

SST reprinted You're Living All Over Me with the corrected name.

years.big: I guess I'll have to do it.
years.h: Mascis hits Barlow with his guitar at a Connecticut club
years.p: During Severed Lips, Barlow makes bass feedback instead of playing his parts. Mascis, sure Murph is about to beat Barlow up, crosses the stage and swings.
years.xp:
Mascis told Michael Azerrad he thought, "I think Murph's going to beat up Lou," and then decided to do it himself. He noted the collision "made a pretty good sound." After several misses he stalked off shouting that he couldn't take it.

Barlow's answer, as Dangerous Minds prints it: "Can't take what, J? Asshole!" He raised his fists and felt, in his words, psychotically happy. Murph considered pummeling both of them, then just walked off.

years.h: Bug hits No. 1 on the UK indie chart
years.p: Cut at Fort Apache in Cambridge, Massachusetts. It stays on the chart 38 weeks, and Freak Scene reaches No. 4 there.
years.xp:
Mascis wrote the parts for Barlow and Murph and called Bug "the album I'm least happy with of anything I've done."

Barlow on Freak Scene, to Willamette Week: "At the time, I thought it was kind of a cheap shot." He said the band later played the Bug material live often enough that it "killed the bad vibe."

years.h: Barlow screams the last track of Bug until he coughs blood
years.p: He sings only the closer, Don't, shouting one line over and over. He told Willamette Week it wasn't deep-red blood, just an irritated throat.
years.xp: Barlow, on why the song stung: "J wrote this fucking nasty song for me to sing, and it was obviously such a dig."

eras.title: The bassist goes, the major label arrives
eras.text: Mascis eased Barlow out without quite saying so, and Barlow answered on record for years. Dinosaur Jr. signed to Sire, made Green Mind nearly alone, and landed on the biggest alternative tours of the early nineties.

q: I've never had such a visceral reaction to a cover version.
years.h: Dinosaur Jr. keeps its Cure cover instead of giving it away
years.p: They cut Just Like Heaven for a compilation and liked it too much to hand over. [[Robert Smith|7d1a1624-784b-4f89-8ff9-b9b493cd059d]] says the cassette J Mascis sent him changed how The Cure play the song live.
years.xp: It came out as a UK single in 1989 and in the U.S. in 1990. Smith's account to Magnet: "J. Mascis sent me a cassette, and it was so passionate. It was fantastic."

years.big: J just seemed really sick of me and Murph.
years.h: Barlow learns through the grapevine that the band carries on
years.p: Barlow said that of Mascis during the Bug sessions. In mid-1989 Mascis and Murph came to his house and he heard a breakup; a tour with a new bassist and a Warner deal were already set.
years.xp:
Murph did most of the talking at the house. When Barlow found out the band was continuing, he confronted both of them, screaming about not being told. That ended the original lineup.

Barlow put his energy into [[Sebadoh|d98c8149-0c01-4151-93e1-48fdc3d5027f]].

years.h: A Sub Pop single with members of Gumball
years.p: Mascis and Murph cut The Wagon with [[Don Fleming|deae7f43-894e-45f1-ae34-08bc0c921b82]] and Jay Spiegel of Gumball. [[Donna Dresch|a192432c-67e4-4eef-af43-25c6fb901a7b]] had played bass on an Australian tour.

years.h: Sire Records gets Dinosaur Jr.
years.p: The major-label deal that had been lined up while Barlow was being pushed out is signed.

years.h: Green Mind is mostly Mascis alone
years.p: The major-label debut on Blanco y Negro/Sire. Murph barely plays; Mascis handles most of the drums himself and overdubs the rest.
years.xp:
Dangerous Minds describes it as essentially a Mascis solo record: guitar, bass and drums on most tracks, with Murph on only a few. Mascis believed arranging the drums mattered more than the guitar.

The mix runs from rockers like The Wagon to acoustic-driven songs like Puke + Cry and Thumb.

years.h: Barlow answers on Sebadoh III, starting with The Freed Pig
years.p: Lou Barlow's first big Sebadoh album opens with a song about his treatment in Dinosaur Jr. and his anger at J Mascis.

years.h: Van Conner fills in, then Mike Johnson takes the bass
years.p: Johnson stays until 1997. [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] supports Dinosaur Jr. on tour in 1991.
years.xp: Hypebot has the band touring Europe with Sonic Youth and Nirvana that year, and appearing in the tour film 1991: The Year Punk Broke.

years.h: A UK package tour called Rollercoaster
years.p: Dinosaur Jr. shares the bill with [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]], [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]] and [[Blur|ba853904-ae25-4ebb-89d6-c44cfbd71bd2]].

years.h: Where You Been lands in the UK top 10
years.p: Murph is back on most of the drums, Mike Johnson on bass and harmonies. Start Choppin' reaches the UK top 20 and Out There gets 120 Minutes rotation.

q: The worst touring experience I've ever had.
years.h: Three shows a week at Lollapalooza, in the hottest days of the summer
years.p: Dinosaur Jr. plays the 1993 tour. Mascis later told Magnet he didn't like any of the other bands.
years.xp: Mascis to Magnet: "We only played three days a week, those days being the hottest of that summer."

years.h: Murph quits, and Mascis is the last original member
years.p: After the Where You Been tour, Murph leaves. George Berz drums live; Murph joins [[The Lemonheads|58a53082-a629-4ff1-a44d-7492d6f6e8fb]] in 1995.
years.xp: Mascis, on Lollapalooza: "Murph was really freaked out by all of it and had to quit when it was over."

eras.title: A hit single, then daytime TV
eras.text: With Murph gone, Mascis did most of the work in the studio, with Mike Johnson on bass. It produced the band's biggest single, then faded on a label that barely promoted the last record.

years.h: Feel the Pain gives them their biggest single
years.p: Without a Sound reaches No. 4 on U.S. Alternative Airplay and No. 25 in the UK. In the Spike Jonze video, Mascis and Mike Johnson play golf across New York.

years.h: Almost no push behind Hand It Over
years.p: Mascis said the record had no hit single. Take a Run at the Sun reaches No. 53 in the UK on some editions.

yt: Never Bought It on Jenny Jones
years.h: They tape The Jenny Jones Show days before the end
years.p: On November 6, after playing Tramps in New York, Mascis, Mike Johnson and drummer George Berz tape Never Bought It and Out There. The host calls the second one Outta There.
years.xp:
Dangerous Minds calls it a very weird venue for the band, a talk show built on strippers, feuding neighbors and paternity tests. A few days later the band played the Middle East in Boston, its final show in that form.

Low turnout on tour and little label push ended it. Mascis went solo as J Mascis + The Fog.

eras.title: Tapes back, grudge gone
eras.text: Mascis took his time, then did the two things that made a reunion possible: he got the SST masters back, and he started turning up at Barlow's shows.

years.h: Mascis starts showing up at Sebadoh gigs
years.p: He also puts out the first of two albums as J Mascis + The Fog. Barlow realizes Mascis doesn't hold a grudge.
years.xp: Barlow in 2005: once he saw Mascis wasn't avoiding him out of dislike, J became more human to him.

years.h: Mascis and Mike Watt play two London shows with the Asheton brothers
years.p: They play Stooges songs with [[Ron Asheton|a10c8616-cdc3-4fd1-a0fa-bc35a6514168]] and [[Scott Asheton|8ff201f8-3b3f-40dd-a7f7-8d0a2184c62e]]; the billing is Asheton, Asheton, Mascis and Watt.

years.h: Mascis wins back the first three albums from SST
years.p: He regains the master rights and sets up reissues on Merge Records for early 2005.

years.cap: The reunited trio at Leeds Festival, August 2005
years.h: The original trio returns, live on The Late Late Show
years.p: Mascis, Barlow and Murph play Craig Ferguson's show, their first time together since 1989. A European tour follows in June.
years.xp:
Asked what changed, Mascis said they chilled out; Barlow said they grew up.

In May, Barlow's mother organized an autism benefit at Smith College in Northampton, and Mascis and Barlow played a set as Deep Wound.

eras.title: More albums than the first time
eras.text: The reunion was supposed to be a tour. It turned into more albums than the original trio made the first time, from three people who still barely talk off stage.

years.h: Their gear gets stolen outside a New York hotel
years.p: Much of the equipment is taken during a New York stop. The same year, the band curates an All Tomorrow's Parties festival.

years.cap: Dinosaur Jr. at Where The Action Is, Stockholm, June 14, 2008
years.h: Beyond puts Barlow back on a Dinosaur Jr. record as a writer
years.p: The first trio album of new songs since Bug, and Barlow's first songwriting since You're Living All Over Me. It debuts at No. 69 and Pitchfork gives it 8.4.
years.xp:
Barlow got two songs, Back to Your Heart and Lightning Bulb. "I was very happy to get two songs on the album," he told Magnet.

The reunion tour did well enough that, in Barlow's words, a new record felt like "the next logical thing to do."

years.cap: Lou Barlow at The Riot Room, Kansas City, October 26, 2009
years.h: Farm gives them their highest U.S. chart peak
years.p: No. 29 on the Billboard 200 after a June 23 release on Jagjaguwar. Recorded at Mascis's house, it's heavier and closer to Where You Been. They play Pieces on Jimmy Fallon two days later.

years.h: I Bet on Sky makes it three since the reunion
years.p: Out in September on Jagjaguwar, to favorable reviews.

years.h: "We're not chatting," Barlow says of Mascis
years.p: Barlow tells NME that music is the glue between them. Murph says he's the go-between and the other two email once in a blue moon.
years.xp:
Barlow: "J. makes me laugh. He's incredibly dry and has a pretty harsh sense of humor that I enjoy."

Murph: "J. will text me asking, 'Do you want to see if Lou will do this?'" He called the arrangement "a total Spinal Tap moment."

years.h: The fourth reunion album, Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not
years.p: Jagjaguwar puts it out the day after NME runs Barlow's remarks about Mascis.
play: Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not

years.h: Over Your Shoulder finds a Japanese TV audience 25 years late
years.p: The song from Without a Sound reaches No. 18 on Japan's Billboard chart, apparently because of its use on Gachinko Fight Club.

years.h: Sweep It Into Space waits a year for COVID
years.p: Album twelve was due in mid-2020. I Ran Away and Garden came out first.

years.h: The band's story gets a feature documentary, Freakscene
years.p: Freakscene: The Story of Dinosaur Jr. runs from Deep Wound to the reunion.

years.cap: J Mascis with Dinosaur Jr. at The Stone Pony, Asbury Park, New Jersey, January 24, 2024
years.h: There Near becomes album thirteen
years.p: Announced in June with the single Several Got Away; out August 28 on Jagjaguwar.
